    17  /-!
    18  # Rank of matrices
    19  
    20  The rank of a matrix `A` is defined to be the rank of range of the linear map corresponding to `A`.
    21  This definition does not depend on the choice of basis, see `Matrix.rank_eq_finrank_range_toLin`.
    22  
    23  ## Main declarations
    24  
    25  * `Matrix.rank`: the rank of a matrix
    26  * `Matrix.cRank`: the rank of a matrix as a cardinal
    27  * `Matrix.eRank`: the rank of a matrix as a term in `ℕ∞`.
    28  
    29  ## Main results
    30  
    31  * `Matrix.rank_eq_finrank_range_toLin`: the rank equals the dimension of the range of the
    32  corresponding linear map, and is therefore independent of the choice of bases.
    33  * `Matrix.rank_eq_finrank_span_cols`, `Matrix.rank_eq_finrank_span_row`: the rank equals the
    34  dimension of the space spanned by the columns (resp. rows).
    35  * `Matrix.rank_transpose`: transposing a matrix does not change its rank.
    36  * `Matrix.rank_mul_le`: the rank of `A * B` is at most the rank of `A` and at most the rank of `B`.
    37  * `Matrix.rank_mul_eq_left_of_isUnit_det`, `Matrix.rank_mul_eq_right_of_isUnit_det`: multiplying by
    38  an invertible matrix does not change the rank.
    39  * `Matrix.exists_rank_normal_form`: every square matrix over a field can be brought, by left and
    40  right multiplication by invertible matrices, into the block form `fromBlocks 1 0 0 0`, where the
    41  identity block has size equal to the rank of the matrix.
    42  -/

    47  
    48  namespace Matrix
    49  
    50  open Module Cardinal Set Submodule
